transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio says there is no information that a series of outages
and technical failures across the U.S. are related to each other or to a malign actor.
We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances
have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another
nation-state, with a malign actor of any kind.
Again, we have no evidence of that.
We have no indications of that.
We have no reason to believe that.
Rubio is traveling with President Trump as they prepare for key meetings with Chinese
President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China.
Trump is facing criticism, including among fellow Republicans, after the service outages
that have snarled air travel, cut off work, limited bank access, and disrupted classified
communications.
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang signaled interest in returning to lead the computer chip company
after he resigned following revelations of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, but
the board's chair says the company does not intend to reinstate him.
Meanwhile, Huang has agreed to appear before Congress, and appears Shannon Bond reports
he'll face scrutiny over national security scandals swirling around the company.
Jensen Huang and Nvidia's top lawyer will answer questions from the House foreign affairs
and intelligence committees, and the select committee on the Chinese Communist Party in
early December.
The interviews will take place behind closed doors.
Lawmakers say they want answers about Nvidia's role in alleged chip smuggling and efforts
to evade export controls meant to block China from accessing the most advanced U.S. chips.
And they'll ask Huang about his involvement with a woman U.S. intelligence officials say
was recruited by China's top spy agency.
NPR has not independently confirmed those reports.
Shannon Bond, NPR News.
Ukraine struck a strategic bridge linking mainland Russia to the annexed Crimean Peninsula
for the second time in as many days.
Ukraine says the attack is retaliatory for Russia's own targeting of Ukrainian bridges
and other civilian infrastructure, and PR's Charles Maine reports from Moscow.
Ukraine has previously attempted attacks along the 12-mile Kerch Bridge, seen it as both
the physical symbol of Russia's illegal annexation of Crimea in 2014 and a pet project the president
Vladimir Putin.
Yet early Tuesday, according to Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky, a Ukrainian-made
Flamingo missile pierced Russia's air defenses to inflict heavy damage on the structure,
destroying a key support archway and sending a section of road into the sea.
The Moscow-backed authorities in Crimea said two people were killed as a result and ordered
all car traffic across the bridge halted.
The Kremlin spokesman said President Putin had been informed of the attack and vowed
to rebuild the bridge better and stronger than before.
Charles Maine's NPR News, Moscow.
The U.S. stock market dropped again today, as Nvidia and other AI stocks led widespread
losses on Wall Street and the S&P 500 sank 1 percent.
This is NPR News.
President Trump's Board of Peace overseeing the Gaza ceasefire between Israel and Hamas
delivered a bleak report on its progress to the U.N. Security Council.
The report warns that continued delays will doom the chances of restoring peace and stability.
Moscow has continued to launch deadly strikes and block humanitarian aid.
The board says people in Gaza are set to face "another winter intense and rubble."
Amid anxiety about the future of work, NPR's Andrea Shue reports apprenticeships and the
skilled trades are having a moment.
When Trent Parker first became instruction coordinator for the Electrical Trade Center
in Columbus, Ohio, he encountered a high school administrator who thought the center's apprenticeship
program would be appropriate for kids who were flunking out.
Now with AI threatening many white-collar professions, Parker has seen how the trades
have become highly attractive to people of all backgrounds, including those who went
to college.
"You can see it and feel it.
You talk with parents.
The word is out that college is not the only way to go, that there are other alternatives."
Alternatives that guarantee work.
Enrollment in his apprenticeship has soared in recent years as demand for electricians
has grown.
Andrea Shue and PR News.
Miami is preparing for the much-anticipated arrival of the Grand Theft Auto VI video game,
which is set in Miami-inspired Vice City.
The Miami Heat basketball team will wear black and pink Vice City jerseys tomorrow, the eve
of the video game's release.
The game's developer, Rockstar, commissioned a series of murals, many in the Wynwood neighborhood,
known worldwide for its street art.
This is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Marco Rubio says no evidence links recent U.S. service outages to hackers or a malign actor
Jensen Huang signals interest in returning as Nvidia CEO; board says no reinstatement planned
Jensen Huang and Nvidia's top lawyer to face closed-door House committee questions in December
Ukraine strikes Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Crimea for second time in two days
U.S. stocks fall again as Nvidia and other AI stocks lead losses; S&P 500 down 1%
Trump's Gaza Board of Peace warns U.N. Security Council ceasefire progress is failing
Skilled trades and apprenticeships gain popularity amid AI threats to white-collar jobs, Ohio program shows
Miami Heat to wear Vice City jerseys ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI release
